rv.q: Too simplistic for adults to enjoy as a comedy, yet perhaps too modernised and moralistic to resonate with younger audiences, it falls into an uncomfortable middle ground between a traditional family pantomime and an adult show.
Original, stylish, inclusive, politically cheeky and tremendously entertaining, this is everything a modern pantomime should be.

cn.t: Critics are split on this East London pantomime — one hails its sharp political satire and infectious energy as a standout triumph, while another finds it colourful but unfocused. Strong design and personality shine through despite uneven reception.
